ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.claim: Islahi treats 20:74–76 as a divine insertion: their afterlife register suits God’s majesty, differs from the surrounding speech, and recalls an earlier insertion at 20:53–59.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.anchor: This verse and the two succeeding ones are from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r2.claim: The promised reward is for people who purify themselves ideologically, practically, and morally, following the Qur’an’s guidance about pitfalls and human concessions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r2.anchor: Only they will be eligible to it who will try to purify themselves

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r3.claim: Rejecting the Qur’an’s guidance in pursuit of religious purification leads to extremism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r3.anchor: Rejection of any of these things will lead to extremism in religion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r4.claim: Islahi rejects theologians’ wishful claim that deeds are unimportant: the Qur’an does not promise Paradise on that basis, whose key remains with God; Jewish false hopes are discussed in al-Baqarah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p52/r4.anchor: those who out of their own desire have reduced the importance of deeds, whether they belong or our classical theologians or those of modern times

SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r1.claim: جنات is parsed as an appositive to الدرجات or as an explanatory substitute.

SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects an implied هي جنات, since خالدين would then be a circumstantial phrase without a governing element; with the appositive or explanatory parse, its governor is the implied abiding or the demonstrative meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:20:76/r2.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن يكون التقدير: هي جنات؛ لأن " خالدين " حال.

ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r2.claim: Believers who do good receive lofty stations and eternal gardens with flowing waters; this is the reward of those who attain purity.
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r2.anchor: whereas he who shall appear before Him as a belie ver who has done righteous deeds [59]

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r1.claim: ‘Gardens of Eden’ is either an appositive for ‘the highest ranks’ or an explanatory substitute.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r1.anchor: ( جنات عدن ( بدل من الدرجات العلى أو بيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r2.claim: The river clause is a circumstantial clause modifying the gardens; خالدين فيها is a circumstantial clause modifying the pronoun in لهم, governed by the sense of being established there or by أولئك.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r2.anchor: تجري من تحتها الأنهار ( حال من الجنات وقوله تعالى : ( خالدين فيها ( تحقيق لكون ثوابه تعالى ابقى وهو حال من الضمير في لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r3.claim: The circumstantial clause is understood as a prospective state; Abū al-Baqāʾ rules out making جنات a predicate of an omitted subject because that leaves the circumstantial clause without a governor.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r3.anchor: والحال مقدرة ولا يجوز أن يكون ( جنات ) خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هي جنات لخلو الكلام حينئذ عن عامل في الحال على ما ذكره أبو البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r4.claim: ‘That’ points to their attaining the described triumph; the demonstrative distance conveys exaltation despite the referent’s nearness in the discourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى ما أتيح لهم من الفوز بما ذكر ومعنى البعد لما أشير اليه من قرب من من التفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r5.claim: The one purified is cleansed of unbelief and sins through faith and righteous deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r5.anchor: تطهر من دنس الكفر والمعاصي بما ذكر من الأيمان والأعمال الصالحة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r6.claim: This statement makes explicit what the preceding conditional had implied; mentioning the criminal’s fate first hastens the answer about punishment’s severity and duration in Pharaoh’s challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r6.anchor: وهذا تصريح بما أفادته الشرطية وتقديم ذكر حال المجرم للمسارعة إلى بيان اشدية عذابه عز وجل ودوامه ردا على ما ادعاه فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r7.claim: Some say the conditional passage beginning here is God’s speech, contrasting Pharaoh’s evil with the magicians’ good; al-Ālūsī prefers it as the magicians’ speech, against al-Nīsābūrī’s view.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن الشرطيتين إلى هنا ابتداء كلام منه وجل زعلا تنبيها على قبح ما فعل فرعون وحسن ما فعل السحرة والأول أولى خلافا لما حسبه النيسابوري

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that a major sinner is a criminal—the root suggests cutting fruit, then came to mean committing something reprehensible—and every criminal is assigned hell, so the threat is certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.anchor: استدل المعتزلة بالشرطية الأولى على القطع بعذاب مرتكب الكبيرة قالوا : مرتكب الكبيرة مجرم لأن اصل الجرم قطع الثمرة عن الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.claim: Sunnis reject the premise that ‘criminal’ here includes a major sinner: the Qur’an often uses it for unbelievers, as in the people questioned about Saqar and those who mocked believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.anchor: واجاب أهل السنة بانا لا نسلم الصغرى لجواز أن يراد بالمجرم الكافر فكثيرا ما جاء في القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.claim: Even granting the first premise, they say the rule applies only absent forgiveness; they also deny that the conditional particle is certainly universal, so a categorical threat does not follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.anchor: وعلى تقدير تسليم هذه المقدمة لانسلم الكبرى على اطلاقها وإنما هي كلية بشرط عدم العفو مع انا لا نسلم أن من الشرطية قطعية في العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r3.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r3.claim: If both premises are granted, they are opposed by the promise to a believer who has done good works: a major sinner remains within that promise, contrary to the Muʿtazilite intermediate position.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r3.anchor: وعلى تقدير تسليم المقدمتين يقال يعارض ذلك الدليل عموم الوعد في قوله تعالى ومن يأته مؤمنا الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.claim: They reject the intermediate station between faith and unbelief and argue that accountable people are either believers or unbelievers, so major sinners cannot be excluded from the promise on that basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.anchor: فاذا قالوا : مرتكب الكبيرة على يقال له مؤمن كما لا يقال كافر لاثباتهم المنزلة بين المنزلتين فلا يدخل ذلك في العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r5.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r5.claim: Even if the promise excludes major sinners, reserving the highest ranks and Eden gardens for the righteous implies other, lesser ranks and gardens for sinful believers; there is no basis to distinguish them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r5.anchor: يقال : أن قوله تعالى ( فأولئك ) لهم الدرجات العلى يدل على حصول العفو لاصحاب الكبائر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد؛ رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r6.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet saying that people beneath the highest ranks see their inhabitants like a bright star in the sky, and that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar are among them; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r6.anchor: ولقد أخرج أبو داود وابن مردويه عن أبى سعيد قال : قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) : إن أهل الدرجات العلى ليراهم من تحتهم كما ترون الكوكب الدرى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as interpreting ‘whoever purifies himself’ as whoever says ‘There is no god but God,’ meaning one purified of unbelief; al-Ālūsī uses this to support inclusion of a major sinner in the promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r7.anchor: واستدل على شمول ( من ياته مؤمنا ) صاحب الكبيرة بقوله تعالى ( وذلك جزاء من تزكى ) بناء على ما روى عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بمن تزكى من قال لا اله إلا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r8.claim: The gardens of Eden are everlasting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r8.anchor: {جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r9.claim: The purified person has cleansed himself of sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r9.anchor: أي: تطهر من الذنوب. وقال الكلبي:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r10.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r10.claim: Al-Kalbī says the person purified his soul by affirming there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أعطى زكاة نفسه وقال لا إله إلا الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r1.claim: Gardens of Eden is an appositive for the degrees mentioned immediately before.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r1.anchor: بدل من الدرجات. { تجرى من تحتها الأنهار

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r2.claim: The abiding phrase is circumstantial; its governor is either the demonstrative's meaning or the notion of abiding there.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r2.anchor: حال والعامل فيها معنى الإشارة أو الاستقرار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r3.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself of the stains of unbelievers and sins.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r4.claim: The three preceding verses may be the sorcerers' words, or the beginning of God's own speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:76/r4.anchor: والآيات الثلاث يحتمل أن تكون من كلام السحرة وأن تكون ابتداء كلام من الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r6.claim: The Gardens of Eden are prepared for permanent residence, with the conditions for dwelling already provided.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r7.claim: Rivers flow beneath the gardens' rooms, beds, and grounds; wherever a river is desired, one flows.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r7.anchor: أي من تحت غرفها وأسرتها وأرضها ؛ فلا يراد موضع منها لأن يجري فيه نهر إلا جرى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r8.claim: The people of the gardens, like the gardens themselves, are prepared for permanent residence.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r9.claim: The syntax supplies an omitted antecedent: that immense lasting bliss is the reward of those who purified themselves through faith and righteous deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r9.anchor: أن التقدير : ذلك الجزاء العظيم والنعيم المقيم جزاء الموصوفين , لتزكيتهم أنفسهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r10.claim: This promise consoles the Companions for the persecution they faced when the sūra was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r10.anchor: وفي هذا تسلية للصحابة رضوان الله عليهم فيما كان يفعل بهم عند نزول هذه السورة

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r1.claim: Gardens of Eden is an apposition to the lofty ranks; the flowing-river clause is circumstantial to the gardens, and abiding is circumstantial to those for whom the reward is established or indicated.

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r2.claim: The streams run beneath the dwellings of the gardens or beneath their trees.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r2.anchor: يوسته ميرود از زير منازل آن يا أشجار آن جويها

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r3.claim: That refers to the reward just described. Jazāʾ can repay good or bad, by contract or otherwise; ajr is contractual or analogous and used only for benefit.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r3.anchor: أي : المذكور من الثواب {جزآء من تزكى} الجزاء ما فيه الكفاية من المقابلة

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r4.claim: The reward is for one purified from disbelief and sin through faith and righteous acts, confirming that God’s recompense endures.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى جزاء من تطهر من دنس الكفر والمعاصي بما ذكر من الإيمان والأعمال الصالحة وهذا تحقيق لكون ثواب الله تعالى أبقى

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r5.claim: A hadith compares the lofty ranks visible from below to a shining star in the sky and counts Abu Bakr and Umar among their people.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن أهل الدرجات العلى ليراهم من تحتهم كما ترون الكوكب الدري في أفق السماء وإن أبا أبكر وعمر منهم

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r6.claim: One view says neither the Quran nor established reports confirm that Pharaoh carried out the punishment he threatened against the believers.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r6.anchor: قالوا ليس في القرآن أن فرعون فعل بأولئك المؤمنين ما أوعدهم به ولم يثبت في الأخبار

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for the report that they were magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r7.anchor: قال في "التفسير الكبير" : نقلا عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كانوا أول النهار سحرة وآخره شهداء

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r8.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r8.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum says they began the day unbelievers and ended it righteous martyrs.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r8.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" أصبحوا كفرة وامسوا أبرارا شهداء

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r9.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r9.claim: The Mathnawi recounts that the magicians honored Moses by inviting him to cast first; the cited reports support their martyrdom and Pharaoh’s use of crucifixion.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r9.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : ساحران در عهد فرعون لعين ون مرى كردند با موسى بكين ليك موسى را مقدم داشتند

BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r10.claim: One should choose God, purify the self of blameworthy and satanic traits, adopt spiritual and divine qualities, and give wealth and life to attain the highest opening.
BURSEVI:v5p313#2/r10.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يختار الله تعالى ويتزكى عن الأخلاق الذميمة النفسانية والأوصاف الشنيعة الشيطانية ويتحلى بالأخلاق الروحانية الربانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.claim: The warning about the criminal and the reward for believers interrupts the magicians’ story before the exodus account, serving as admonition and confirmation of the believers’ words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.anchor: هذه الجمل معترضة بين حكاية قصة السحرة وبين ذكر قصة خروج بني إسرائيل ، ساقها الله موعظة وتأييدا لمقالة المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.claim: An alternative says the warning is spoken by Pharaoh’s believing magicians, but Ibn ʿĀshūr finds that unlikely because their speech is not similarly narrated elsewhere in parallel versions of the story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.anchor: وقيل : هي من كلام أولئك المؤمنين . ويبعده أنه لم يحك نظيره عنهم في نظائر هذه القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r12.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr refers back to his explanation of ʿAdn gardens and rivers flowing beneath them at 9:72.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r12.anchor: وتقدم معنى { عدن } وتفسير { تجري من تحتها الأنهار } في قوله تعالى : { وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.claim: One group says these verses are the sorcerers' admonition to Pharaoh, explaining their choice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.anchor: قالت فرقة هذه الآية بجملتها من كلام السحرة لفرعون على جهة الموعظة له والبيان فيما فعلوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.claim: Another says God addresses Muhammad here to show Pharaoh's evil, the sorcerers' virtue, and a warning through the story.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل هي من كلام الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم تنبيها على قبح ما فعل فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r8.claim: Tazakkā means obey God and choose the purest acts; the word plainly carries the sense of acquisition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r8.anchor: وتزكى معناه أطاع الله تعالى وأخذ بأزكى الأمور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309#3/r1.claim: The reward is the recompense for one who purifies himself from disbelief and sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309#3/r1.anchor: وذلك يعني الثواب جزاء من تزكى أي تطهر من الكفر والمعاصي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r1.claim: Gardens of Eden means a permanent abode and is in apposition to the lofty degrees promised in the preceding verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r1.anchor: وقوله: {جنات عدن تجري} أي: إقامة وهو بدل من الدرجات العلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r2.claim: The people of these gardens remain there forever.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r3.claim: This is the reward of one who purifies himself from stain, evil, and shirk, worships God alone, and believes the messengers' reports and commands.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p307/r3.anchor: وذلك جزاء من تزكى} أي: طهر نفسه من الدنس والخبث والشرك

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r10.claim: The highest ranks are explained as lasting gardens of residence, with rivers flowing beneath their trees and buildings.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r10.anchor: جنات عدن إقامة، يعني دائمة تجري من تحتها الأنهار يجري الماء في الأنهار تحت أشجارها وأبنيتها

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r11.claim: Those who purify themselves from disbelief and sins are rewarded, showing that reward comes through deeds.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r11.anchor: وذلك جزاء من تزكى قيل: تطهر من الكفر والمعاصي، فبين أنه يعطي بالأعمال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r5.claim: تزكى means to purify oneself from the stains of sins.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains تزكى as saying لا إله إلا الله.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : قال لا إله إلا الله

MUQATIL:20:74-76/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r4.claim: Rivers flow beneath the gardens, whose inhabitants never die; enduring there is the reward of those who purify themselves.
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r4.anchor: { جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار } يعني تحت البساتين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r1.claim: “Gardens of Eden” is an appositive explaining the preceding “degrees.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r2.claim: The rivers flow beneath the gardens, where their inhabitants remain forever.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r2.anchor: تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r3.claim: The one who purifies himself here is one who leaves polytheism by professing that there is no god but God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r3.anchor: تطهر من الشرك بقوله لا إله إلا الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r4.claim: One view takes these three verses as the two magicians’ statement.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r4.anchor: قيل هذه الآيات الثلاث حكاية قولهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r5.claim: He prefers reading the three verses as God’s direct statement rather than a quotation of the magicians.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#4/r5.anchor: قيل خبر من الله تعالى لا على وجه الحكاية وهو أظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r21.claim: Gardens of Eden explain and stand in apposition to the elevated degrees; عدن means residence.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r21.anchor: { جنات عدن } بيان للدرجات وبدل منها، والعدن الإقامة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r22.claim: Rivers beneath the chambers and couches are rivers of wine, honey, milk, and water.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r22.anchor: أي من تحت غرفها وسررها { الأنهار } من الخمر والعسل واللبن والماء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r24.claim: تزكى means purifying oneself of unbelief and sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r24.anchor: أي من تطهر من الكفر والمعاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r25.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r25.claim: If the magicians uttered these descriptions, they may have heard them from Moses or the Israelites in Egypt, including believers from Pharaoh's family.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r25.anchor: ومن قال هذا من قول السحرة قال: لعل السحرة سمعوه من موسى، أو من بني إسرائيل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r26.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r26.claim: Al-Qurṭubī also allows that God inspired the magicians to speak this knowledge when they believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r26.anchor: قلت: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك إلهاما من الله لهم أنطقهم بذلك لما آمنوا والله أعلم.

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r5.claim: The highest ranks promised to believers are explained as Gardens of Eden with rivers flowing beneath them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r5.anchor: فسرها فقال : { جنات عدن تجرى من تحتها الانهار }

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r6.claim: Because the highest ranks are assigned to believers who come with faith and righteous deeds, lesser ranks must belong to others, namely sinful believers whom God pardons.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r6.anchor: فسائر الدرجات التي هي غير عالية لا بد وأن تكون لغيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification here as saying, There is no god but God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : يريد من قال لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons that lesser ranks are not the reward of the purified, so they belong to sinners from the faithful whom God pardons by grace and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r8.anchor: لما دلت هذه الآية على أن الدرجات العالية هي جزاء من تزكى

STUDYQURAN:20:74/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r3.claim: The Quran mentions the Gardens of Eden in several other places.
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r3.anchor: The Gardens of Eden are mentioned in several places in the Quran

TAB-FULL:v16p120/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r1.claim: The high ranks are Gardens of Eden, permanent dwellings without departure or end; rivers run under the trees and inhabitants remain there forever.
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r1.anchor: يعني: جنات إقامة لا ظعن عنها ولا نفاد لها ولا فناء

TAB-FULL:v16p120/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r2.claim: Jannāt is nominative by apposition to al-darajāt, the high ranks mentioned in the preceding verse.
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r2.anchor: فالجنات من قوله {جنات عدن} [التوبة: 72] مرفوعة بالرد على الدرجات

TAB-FULL:v16p120/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the high ranks promised to believers as Eden.
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى} [طه: 75] قال: عدن

TAB-FULL:v16p120/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r4.claim: The rivers flow beneath the trees in the Gardens.
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r4.anchor: {تجري من تحتها الأنهار} [البقرة: 25] يقول: تجري من تحت أشجارها الأنهار

TAB-FULL:v16p120/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r5.claim: Their stay in the gardens has no defined endpoint.
TAB-FULL:v16p120/r5.anchor: {خالدين فيها} [البقرة: 162] يقول: ماكثين فيها إلى غير غاية محدودة

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r7.claim: Tazakki means growing through sound growth: living with true belief and righteous action.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r7.anchor: والتزكي هو التنمي بالنماء الصالح والمراد به أن يعيش الإنسان باعتقاد حق وعمل صالح

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r8.claim: The verses contrast the consequences of faith and good works with the criminal’s fate, answering Pharaoh’s threat and promise of reward and closeness.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r8.anchor: والآيات الثلاث الواصفة لتبعة الإجرام والإيمان ناظرة إلى وعيد فرعون ووعده لهم

TABATABAI:20:76-79/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r1.claim: Eternal gardens are the reward for faith and righteous conduct, answering Pharaoh’s promise of payment; the high ranks answer his promise to make them close to him.
TABATABAI:20:76-79/r1.anchor: قابلوا ذلك بأن من يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك - وفي الإشارة البعيدة تفخيم شأنهم - لهم الدرجات العلى

TABRISI:20:74-76/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:74-76/r8.claim: Jannāt ʿadn means gardens of abiding residence.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r8.anchor: جنات عدن } أي إقامة { تجري من تحتها الأنهار

TABRISI:20:74-76/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:74-76/r9.claim: The reward is for one who purifies himself from disbelief and sin through faith and obedience.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r9.anchor: معناه إن الثواب الذي تقدم ذكره جزاء من تطهر بالإيمان والطاعة عن دنس الكفر والمعصية

TABRISI:20:74-76/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:74-76/r10.claim: Another view takes tazakkā as seeking purity by intending obedience and acting on it.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r10.anchor: وقيل: تزكى طلب الزكاء بإرادة الطاعة والعمل بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, reports that people raised in Islam and righteous deeds, untouched by sin until death, will be called at Resurrection, recognize their description, receive a banner, and follow it into the Gardens of Eden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس فيما روى عنه سعيد بن جبير: (لله عباد ولدوا في الإسلام ونشؤا في أعمال البر، لم يخالطوا المعاصي وأهلها حتى ماتوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r8.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r8.claim: The Prophet says people enter Paradise through God’s mercy and receive their ranks according to their deeds; no grading is given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p470/r8.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله-عليه السلام-: "تدخلون الجنة برحمة الله وتقسمون الدرجات بأعمالكم"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn ʿAbbās glossing the purified person as one who professes that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (من قال لا إله إلا الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī gives a similar gloss: the purified person professes that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r2.anchor: لا إله إلا الله) (¬1). ونحو ذلك قال الكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r3.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself of sins through obedience instead of becoming sullied by disobedience, seeking to be virtuous in goodness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p472/r3.anchor: {تزكى} تطهير من الذنوب بالطاعة بدلا من التدنس بالمعاصي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r3.claim: The purified person is cleansed of associationism by saying, “There is no god but God.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r3.anchor: { جزاء من تزكى } تطهر من الشرك بقول: لا إله إلا الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r1.claim: The tafsir says the phrase was already explained in Sūrat Maryam.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r1.anchor: {جنات عدن} [طه: 76] وقد فسرناه في سورة مريم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r2.claim: The rivers are said to have been explained in another passage.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r2.anchor: {تجري من تحتها الأنهار} [طه: 76] وقد فسرنا الأنهار أيضا في غير هذا الموضع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r3.claim: The inhabitants will neither die nor leave Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r4.claim: The one who purifies himself is one who believes.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r4.anchor: {وذلك جزاء من تزكى} [طه: 76] يعني: من آمن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r5.claim: Qatadah says the phrase means one who performs righteous deeds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p268/r5.anchor: وهو في قول قتادة: من عمل صالحا

TABRISI:20:71-72/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r8.claim: جنات عدن must be appositional to the high degrees, not a predicate of an omitted subject, since خالدين فيها is circumstantial; therefore one should not pause at الدرجات العلى.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r8.anchor: يجب أن يكون بدلا من الدرجات ولا يجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

TABRISI:20:71-72/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r9.claim: The high degrees are raised by their preceding adverbial predicate, which predicates of أولئك and governs what follows.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r9.anchor: والدرجات مرتفع بالظرف بلا خلاف بينهم لأن الظرف جرى خبرا على المبتدأ

THALABI:v6p254/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p254/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p254/r2.claim: The one who purifies himself is either righteous or cleansed of disbelief and sins.
THALABI:v6p254/r2.anchor: وذلك جزاء من تزكى أي صلح، وقيل: تطهر من الكفر والمعاصي.

THALABI:v6p254/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p254/r3.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p254/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi explains purification as giving the alms of one's soul and saying there is no god but God.
THALABI:v6p254/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني أعطى زكاة نفسه وقال: لا إله إلا الله.

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r5.claim: Zakā means growth in goodness, as wealth grows through zakat; tazakkī means seeking growth, or, in another gloss, purification.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r5.anchor: والزكاة: النماء في الخير، ومنه: الزكاة؛ لأن المال ينمو بها، والتزكي: طلب الزكا
